subject: History
description: Delhi Sultanate + Vijayanagar + early Mughals spread across difficulty tiers

questions.stem: The founder of the SLAVE dynasty (Mamluk dynasty) of the Delhi Sultanate was:
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave / Mamluk dynasty in 1206 after Muhammad Ghori's death. He began the Qutub Minar. Iltutmish (his son-in-law) consolidated it; Razia was his daughter; Balban later raised its stature.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The VIJAYANAGAR empire was founded in 1336 by:
questions.explanation: Brothers Harihara I and Bukka I — on the advice of their guru Vidyaranya — founded the Vijayanagar empire on the banks of the Tungabhadra in 1336. Krishnadeva Raya (r. 1509-1529) was its most famous ruler, during whom the empire reached its zenith.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which Delhi-Sultanate ruler shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and then BACK again — a disastrous transfer of population?
questions.explanation: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq (r. 1325-1351) ordered the 1327 forced relocation of Delhi's entire population to Devagiri (renamed Daulatabad). Water scarcity and administrative chaos forced reversal. His token-currency experiment (copper tokens for silver) was another famous failure.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the BATTLE with its YEAR. A. First Battle of Panipat. B. Battle of Khanwa. C. Battle of Talikota. D. Second Battle of Panipat. List-II: 1. 1526. 2. 1527. 3. 1556. 4. 1565.
questions.explanation: 1526 — Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi (First Panipat) founding the Mughal empire. 1527 — Babur defeats Rana Sanga (Khanwa). 1556 — Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeat Hemu (Second Panipat). 1565 — Deccan sultanates crush Vijayanagar at Talikota.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The MARKET-CONTROL reforms — fixing prices, maintaining a separate market for each commodity, and appointing a Diwan-i-Riyasat — were introduced by:
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296-1316) introduced elaborate market regulations to sustain his large standing army at fixed low wages. Separate markets for grain, cloth, horses, slaves. Diwan-i-Riyasat was the chief market officer. Ziauddin Barani is the primary source.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Consider the following about the BHAKTI MOVEMENT. 1. Ramananda preached in Hindi in northern India; his disciples included Kabir and Ravidas. 2. Guru Nanak (1469-1539) founded Sikhism and rejected caste and formal ritual. 3. Meerabai was a Krishna-devotee princess of Rajasthan. 4. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu popularised the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition centred on Krishna-devotion in Bengal. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Ramananda's disciple-list included weavers, cobblers, barbers — a radical democratisation. Nanak's janamsakhis recount his travels. Meerabai's bhajans to Giridhar Gopal are still sung. Chaitanya's sankirtan style (congregational Hari-kirtan) still shapes ISKCON.

questions.stem: The IQTA system in the Delhi Sultanate refers to:

options.option_text: Revenue-assignment grants to nobles in lieu of salary

questions.explanation: Iqta = territorial assignment whose land-revenue supported the noble (iqtadar) who held it. Used from Iltutmish onwards to pay nobles, soldiers and governors without cash salaries. Non-hereditary — the Sultan could transfer/revoke the iqta at will. Firoz Shah Tughlaq made iqtas de-facto hereditary; that weakened central control.
